name: final-training-monitoring
purpose: We want to see how our agent changes over the whole final training run, milestone by milestone. Our first monitoring used the 40 classic development worlds, and that turned out to be far too noisy: the score interval was about 0.9 points wide, while the training logs showed a steady gain of about 0.24 points over 2,000 episodes that the evaluation could not see. So every milestone is now also played on 100 fresh classic worlds, next to coin-heaven and loot-crate for retention.

what_we_evaluate.checkpoints: the untrained reference and every retained milestone of all six jobs, every 2,000 episodes
what_we_evaluate.never: the held-out suite holdout-rule-based. The evaluator refuses it and refuses any registration that reuses its worlds.

suite.name: classic-monitoring-100
suite.seed_audit: I checked all 100 seeds, and their +1,000,000 offsets, against every integer in the 908 tracked text files on 17 September, leaving out digit runs inside hex hashes. Nothing collides and nothing lies anywhere near the block. The block does not overlap the loop-guard test worlds 960000001-960000100.

how_we_use_it: This is monitoring on development worlds. We may look at it as often as we like, and we will use it to rank candidates when we choose the checkpoint to ship. The number we report for the shipped agent comes from the held-out suite, read once, after the choice is made.
known_limits: Opponents are not seeded, so the same classic world still plays out differently between checkpoints.
Six replicas per milestone. Differences between replicas stay large, so arm-level claims need the hierarchical intervals.
cost_per_milestone: 6 checkpoints x (100 + 40 + 40) = 1,080 games, roughly 45 to 60 minutes on a laptop with two jobs
